headline: The New York Fed's president says the AI chip shortage will probably last more than two years, after a sharp rise in the cost of chips.
score_reason: Lowered by 1 from 6: the interview took place on 13 Oct 2026, before the window.
importance_line: It affects consumers and businesses facing higher prices for chips and goods that use them, and the view is one official's, relayed by a secondary outlet.
summary: Bloomberg News reports, as relayed by BigGo Finance, that John Williams, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, said in an interview on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 that the AI hardware supply crunch will probably take longer than two years to balance, after a "pretty abrupt and large increase" in the cost of chips and goods that depend on them. He added that he still thinks one more interest-rate rise this year may be appropriate and that many AI backers are "relatively price insensitive", so monetary policy may do little to slow the buildout.
notes: Bloomberg original not read; link is the page where the text was read.
